darwin/arm64.reference: Apple M3, 8 GB, go1.27.2 (every RSS and init gate re-run under go1.27.3 on 2026-10-22 and within its row), release flags (CGO_ENABLED=0 -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w")
darwin/arm64.set_from: measured 2026-10-13 on the P-06 tree (archive 85.1.2); RSS rows (entries, case_budgets): the highest median, per row, over seven macos-latest (macos-26-arm64) runs of the Perf gates (macos) job on 2026-10-24 under go1.27.3, each run's own reading the median of nine through the reaper: runs 40126431364 (job 120968759111, 9392bc12), 40128808970 (job 120975905457, d34f308b), 40129385436 (job 120977636340, b46e7983), 40130432262 (job 120980799149, 5412da25), 40130933466 (job 120982296926, efd9d1ef), 40132141210 (job 120985922052, 2a588b9a) and 40132781426 (job 120987866745, PR #95 head 32cacffd, the failure that prompted this). The seven are the lane-g/linux-rss (PR #93) heads and the PR #95 head; none differs from main 323e4075 in anything the release binary builds: they differ in test files, test/perf/budgets.json, internal/budget/budgets_gen.go, two fuzz seeds, internal/fault/fault_on.go (built only under the rashomonfault tag) and, on 32cacffd, a separate module pgraph/ that nothing imports; 9392bc12's rss_test.go predates the nine-readings and TestRES28p_ changes and logs at :389 and :428 instead of :433 and :472, with the same measurement. The reference rows above read lower than the runner: it reads 0.3 to 1.0 MiB higher on every entry (recap.pending 6.06 against 6.75 to 6.98, recap.stop 7.06 against 7.81 to 7.95), and hook.400B, hook.40KB and post.1MiB read above their RES-28 lines, so a row cannot be taken from this repository's Apple M3. gate.go gates a platform whose maps are non-empty only on the rows in them, so all eight entries and all ten cases carry a row here; hook.1MiB, hook.4MiB, hook.8MiB, post.40KB, post.540B, post.4MiB and post.8MiB read at or below RES-28's line on the runner, and their rows here are still the highest runner median, not the line. p95 equals p50, as on linux/amd64 (information only). Within a run the hook 1, 4 and 8 MiB readings carry an occasional outlier (hook.4MiB as low as 15.70, hook.8MiB as low as 23.89, in one or two of nine; hook.1MiB as high as 10.17), but no run's median left the band across the seven (hook.1MiB 9.19 to 9.86, hook.4MiB 19.52 to 19.70, hook.8MiB 31.78 to 31.95), so no row sits on a mode; a median that did land on the low mode reads under its row, which no gate fails

linux/amd64.set_from: RSS rows (entries, case_budgets): medians over twelve ubuntu-latest runs of this job, the runs between 39868535027 and 39987323280 on 2026-10-22 and 23 under go1.27.3, each run's own reading the median of nine through the reaper; the small entries and cases read 8.11 to 8.31 MiB in all twelve, which is 3 MiB above the 5.0 this repository's reference Linux VM reads, so a row cannot be taken from any other machine. Two readings are bimodal across runs and their rows sit on the high mode so that both pass: post.edit_314k read 8.12 to 8.24 in six runs and 10.13 to 10.24 in six (row 10.17), recap.pending 8.24 to 8.54 in eleven and 10.26 in one (row 10.26); the cause of the 2 MiB step is not established. recap.stop reads 10.33 to 10.46 in all twelve (row 10.39): schema 5's larger call record (96d968d3) cost 0.5 MiB on the reference VM between 818ee5ea and 96d968d3 (6.11 to 6.63 MiB) and more on ubuntu-latest. hook.edit_50k lowered from 9.67 to 8.16 and every other row moved up by 0.4 to 0.6 MiB with the binary's growth since 739e94c. The cases hook.1MiB, hook.4MiB, hook.8MiB, post.1MiB, post.4MiB and post.8MiB are the median of nine through the reaper in one ubuntu-latest run of this job, 40123234728 (job 120959121636, 2026-10-24, go1.27.3), the reading TestRES28_ printed in its failure: hook 10.51, 19.05 and 27.35 MiB, post 10.39, 16.86 and 24.58 MiB. They are one run each, not the twelve the other rows are, and the nine readings inside that run are bimodal for the 4 and 8 MiB hook cases (16.5 to 16.6 and 20.6 to 21.2 for hook.4MiB; 24.8 to 25.6 and 31.0 to 33.4 for hook.8MiB), so the 4 and 8 MiB rows are to be re-taken from further runs. hook.1MiB and post.1MiB are re-set on the high mode, the convention of post.edit_314k and recap.pending: the 1 MiB readings are bimodal in about 2 MiB steps (low 10.25 to 10.52, high 12.27 to 12.46). hook.1MiB read a median of 10.51 in run 40123234728 (job 120959121636), a median of 10.51 in #95 job 120972630305 (readings 12.44 10.52 10.30 10.25 10.51 12.31 10.26 12.43 10.48, three high), and a median of 12.29 in #94 job 120976183984 (readings 12.36 10.38 12.46 12.31 10.49 12.36 12.29 10.50 10.48, five high, which failed the 10.51 row at +10 percent); its row is the highest high-mode reading, 12.46, from that job. post.1MiB read 10.39 in run 40123234728, 10.39 in #95 job 120972630305 (readings 10.39 10.39 10.26 12.27 10.51 10.46 10.36 10.26 12.36, two high) and 10.46 in #94 job 120976183984 (readings 10.26 10.47 10.46 12.35 10.39 10.46 10.29 10.50 10.35, one high); its median has not yet landed in the high mode, so its row 12.36, the highest high-mode reading (#95), is a precaution based on the observed high-mode readings, since the same payload size shows the same step and a median needs only five of nine high. The 4 and 8 MiB rows are not moved: no run has shown five of nine readings in a high mode for them (hook.8MiB in #95 read 33.16 and 33.29 in two of nine, hook.4MiB read 16.6 to 17.1 in #95 and #94, post.4MiB 14.2 and 16.3, post.8MiB 22.4 and 24.6), and the +10 percent the gate allows covers the post rows entirely; hook.4MiB (row 19.05, gate 20.96, high mode near 21) stays on watch. hook.8MiB is re-set on the high mode, the convention of hook.1MiB and post.1MiB: #95 job 120980919989 (81f38ab3) read a median of 31.20 (readings 25.28 33.14 22.95 33.06 24.92 24.84 33.23 33.25 31.20, five of nine high, which failed the 27.35 row at +10 percent), after #95 read 25.10 25.72 24.86 33.16 33.29 27.43 24.64 24.99 25.12 (two high); its row is the highest high-mode reading CI has observed, 33.29 (#95, earlier run). benchmarks: best of three, -benchtime 20x, from run 39876043270's bench-linux artifact on 323e4075 under go1.27.3, cross-checked on a second linux/amd64 machine within 0.1 percent on 31 of 40 rows, and within 5 percent on all of them
